test: Media persistence across project revisits (rebrand + migration round, 2026-08-07)
method: Local http server, Browser pane (visibilityState=visible). Sequence driven programmatically via chip switches; evidence from the in-page Performance Resource Timing API (duplicate-fetch detection) plus DOM node-identity checks. The Browser pane's own network buffer was unreliable across same-domain reloads, so resource timings were used instead.
sequence: Blackthorn (first open) -> Star (chip switch) -> Blackthorn (chip switch back)
playback_gating_note: While Star was active, only the in-view clip played (paused:false) and the off-screen clips stayed paused, so only the visible project's in-view videos ever play.
conclusion: PASS. Revisiting Blackthorn produced zero second webm/jpg fetches (no request at all): the exact same stack and img DOM nodes are reused, and each media URL was requested exactly once for the whole session. Leaving a project pauses and rewinds its videos to currentTime 0; only the active project's in-view clips play.
